acceptance: An inventory names all imports, documented examples, external compatibility promises, and behavioral dimensions for ConcurrentQueryExecutor, PowerRunExecutor, StreamRunner, and benchmark-specific power harnesses.
ConcurrentQueryExecutor is either a tested compatibility adapter to the canonical throughput API or is deprecated/removed with migration guidance.
PowerRunExecutor is either a tested compatibility adapter to the canonical power harness or is deprecated/removed with migration guidance; it is never represented as throughput-equivalent.
Warmups, iterations, statistics, fail-fast behavior, timeout semantics, result shapes, and error propagation are preserved or explicitly versioned as breaking changes.
Any beta compatibility shim has a named owner, introduction version, removal version, and one migration example.
Regression tests prove that no retained path can report success without executing the requested SQL.
context: This is a follow-up reconciliation, not a repeat of concurrency-executor-consolidation. The earlier item addressed the non-executing stub and broad duplication; this item closes the remaining public semantic ambiguity visible in the current tree.
description:
A completed consolidation item removed a fake-success stub, but the current tree still exposes ConcurrentQueryExecutor and PowerRunExecutor beside the canonical throughput StreamRunner and benchmark-specific power harnesses. Reassess each public or documented utility by behavior, not by the word executor, then route, adapt, deprecate, or remove it.

Decision boundary: ConcurrentQueryExecutor may map to the supported throughput path only after its configuration, warmup, iteration, failure, statistics, and result semantics are inventoried. PowerRunExecutor must map to the canonical power-test harness or be retired; it must not be folded into StreamRunner merely to reduce class count.
